name: Treaty of Fort Stanwix (1768) - Crown boundary line
nations: Grant from Six Nations to King George III and Agreement of Boundary Line at Fort Stanwix, New York
land_description: Grant by the Six Nations to King George III; Fort Stanwix boundary line running from the Ohio/Tennessee region north to the Mohawk Valley. Pre-US instrument included in NARA series.
kappler_cite: n/a (listed in OSU Tribal Treaties Database as 'Treaty of Fort Stanwix, 1768')
notes: Included as context only; NARA RIT 1-7 are colonial/British-era items (1722-1768), not US treaties. Boundary geometry and Six Nations authority over the ceded Ohio-Valley lands are historically contested [from-memory].

name: Treaty with the Delawares (Treaty of Fort Pitt), 1778
nations: Delaware at Fort Pitt
land_description: Alliance and passage through Delaware territory; Delaware territorial rights guaranteed; invitation to other friendly Ohio-Country tribes to join and form a state with representation in Congress.
notes: First treaty between the United States (Continental Congress) and a Native nation. Approved by Congress, not the Senate (pre-Constitution). Wikipedia states the statehood provision was never fulfilled. Stat. page from Stat. vol. 7 index; Kappler page from OSU URL slug.

name: Treaty of Fort Stanwix (1784) - Six Nations
nations: Six Nations at Fort Stanwix
land_description: Boundary line for Six Nations lands; Six Nations relinquished claims west of the line; Oneida and Tuscarora possession confirmed; six square miles around Oswego reserved to US; hostages held.
notes: Seneca and others later disputed the authority of signatories [from-memory]. Articles confirmed via OSU TTD.

name: Treaty of Fort McIntosh, 1785
nations: Wyandot, Delaware, Chippewa, and Ottawa at Fort McIntosh
land_description: Cession of much of present Ohio to the US; boundary line with Wyandot, Delaware, Chippewa, Ottawa.
notes: Land description from memory [from-memory]; Stat./Kappler pages verified.

name: Treaty of Hopewell with the Cherokee, 1785
nations: Cherokee at Hopewell
land_description: Boundaries between Cherokee and US; cession of land around Nashville; Art. XII provision for a Cherokee deputy to Congress.
notes: Wikipedia (pointer) for article content. Georgia and North Carolina contested the boundaries [from-memory].

name: Treaty of Hopewell with the Choctaw, 1786
nations: Choctaw at Hopewell
land_description: Boundaries; small cession for trading posts; US protection.
notes: Acreage per Wikipedia (pointer); verify against treaty text.

name: Treaty of Hopewell with the Chickasaw, 1786
nations: Chickasaw at Hopewell
land_description: Boundaries; reserved trading-post site.

name: Treaty of Fort Finney (Mouth of the Great Miami) with the Shawnee, 1786
nations: Shawnee at the Mouth of the Great Miami River
land_description: Shawnee acknowledged US sovereignty; boundaries in southwestern Ohio.
notes: Land description from memory [from-memory]. Commonly called Fort Finney.

name: Treaty of Fort Harmar with the Wyandot and allied nations, 1789
nations: Wyandot, Delaware, Ottawa, Chippewa, Potawatomi, and Sauk at Fort Harmar
land_description: Reaffirmed Fort McIntosh cessions in Ohio.
notes: Concluded under Confederation authority just before the new government took office; Senate handling of Fort Harmar is in [from-memory]. Western Confederacy rejected the settlement, leading to the Northwest Indian War [from-memory].

name: Treaty of New York with the Creeks, 1790
nations: Creeks at New York
land_description: Boundary lines in Georgia; Creek cession of lands; secret articles (see OSU TTD).
notes: Often described as the first Indian treaty advised and consented to by the Senate under the Constitution [from-memory, verify].

name: Treaty of Holston with the Cherokee, 1791
nations: Cherokee at Holston River, with an additional article of February 17, 1792, at Philadelphia
land_description: Boundary line and cession in present eastern Tennessee; additional article of 1792-02-17 in same NARA file.

name: Treaty of Canandaigua (Pickering Treaty), 1794 - Six Nations
nations: Six Nations at Konondaigua, New York
land_description: Acknowledged Haudenosaunee lands in New York (Oneida, Onondaga, Cayuga reservations; Seneca boundaries); right-of-way road at Fort Schlosser to Lake Erie; $4,500 annual goods (Art. 6).
notes: Still invoked by Haudenosaunee (annual cloth distribution). Senate ratification date not captured (submitted to Senate 1795-01-02 per Wikipedia).

name: Treaty with the Oneida, Tuscarora, and Stockbridge, 1794
nations: Oneida, Tuscarora, and Stockbridge at Oneida, New York
land_description: Acknowledgment of Oneida/Tuscarora/Stockbridge lands in New York; compensation for Revolutionary War losses.
notes: Land description from memory [from-memory]; Oneida 1794 land-claim litigation (Oneida I/II) relates to later NY purchases in violation of the Nonintercourse Act.

name: Treaty of Greenville, 1795
nations: Wyandot, Delaware, Shawnee, Ottawa, Chippewa, Potawatomi, Eel River, Wea, Kickapoo, Piankashaw, and Kaskaskia at Greenville
land_description: Cession of most of present Ohio (Greenville Treaty Line) and part of Indiana; reserved tracts for US posts (including the future Fort Dearborn/Chicago site); created the annuity system; ended the Northwest Indian War.
notes: Wikipedia: Senate ratified 1795-12-22. Acreage not stated in sources read; Royce cession polygons would supply. Ratification detail: 1795-12-22 (Senate) [single-source: Wikipedia only; the extracted 7 Stat. 49 margin reads 'Proclamation, Dec. 2, 1795', possibly an extraction error; confirm against the Senate Executive Journal]

name: Treaty of Colerain with the Creeks, 1796
nations: Creeks at Colerain, Georgia
land_description: Reaffirmed boundaries; provisions on fugitive slaves and trade.
notes: Land/provision description from memory [from-memory].

name: Agreement (Treaty of Big Tree) with the Seneca, 1797
nations: Agreement with Seneca at Genesee, New York
land_description: Seneca sale of most Genesee Country (western NY) except reserved tracts, conveying the pre-emption right holder's interest; US-supervised.
stat_cite: 7 Stat. 601 (Appendix: contract between Robert Morris and Senecas)
notes: NARA lists as 'Agreement with Seneca at Genesee'. Treaty named 'Big Tree' [from-memory]. Stat. cite from Stat. vol. 7 index appendix (p. 601). Kappler page not confirmed.

name: Treaty of Fort Wayne with the Delaware, Shawnee, Potawatomi, Miami, Eel River, Wea, Kickapoo, Piankashaw, Kaskaskia, 1803
nations: Delaware, Shawnee, Potawatomi, Miami, Eel River, Wea, Kickapoo, Piankashaw, and Kaskaskia at Fort Wayne on the Miami of the Lake
land_description: Boundary and cession in Indiana/Illinois; Vincennes tract.
notes: Land description from memory [from-memory].

name: Treaty of St. Louis with the Sauk and Fox, 1804
nations: Sauk and Fox at St. Louis in the District of Louisiana
land_description: Cession of lands in northwestern Illinois, southwestern Wisconsin, eastern Missouri for goods worth $2,234.50 and a $1,000 annuity.
notes: Signatories lacked tribal authority to cede (Wikipedia, pointer); never accepted by Black Hawk. Reaffirmed in 1815 and 1816 (RIT 72, 73, 78). Validity disputed [disputed]. Ratification detail: 1805-01-25 (Senate consent; read from the Stat. margin by V2).

name: Treaty of Fort Industry, 1805
nations: Wyandot, Ottawa, Chippewa, Munsee, Delaware, Shawnee, and Potawatomi at Fort Industry on the Miami of the Lake
land_description: Cession in northern Ohio (Western Reserve / Firelands area).
notes: Land description from memory [from-memory].

name: Treaty of Detroit, 1807
nations: Ottawa, Chippewa, Wyandot, and Potawatomi at Detroit
land_description: Cession of southeastern Michigan and northwestern Ohio lands.
notes: Land description from memory [from-memory].

name: Treaty of Fort Wayne (1809) - Delaware, Potawatomi, Miami, Eel River
nations: Delaware, Potawatomi, Miami, and Eel River at Fort Wayne
land_description: Cession of roughly 2.5 million acres in Indiana (the '10 O'clock line' / Treaty of Fort Wayne cession).
notes: Acreage approx. 2.5 million [from-memory]; Tecumseh's opposition to this treaty fed the Prophetstown conflict [from-memory].

name: Treaty of Fort Jackson (Capitulation of the Creeks), 1814
nations: Creeks at Fort Jackson
land_description: Creek cession of lands in Georgia and central Alabama after the Creek War (including from allied Creeks).
notes: Acreage ~23 million per Wikipedia (pointer). Lands taken from Red Stick and allied Creeks alike.

name: Treaty of Spring Wells, 1815
nations: Wyandot, Delaware, Seneca, Shawnee, Miami, Chippewa, Ottawa, and Potawatomi at Spring Wells near Detroit
land_description: Peace and restoration of pre-war status with Wyandot, Delaware, Seneca, Shawnee, Miami, Chippewa, Ottawa, Potawatomi.
notes: Land description from memory [from-memory].

name: Treaty of St. Louis with the Sauk of Rock River, 1816
nations: Sauk (of Rock River) at St. Louis, Missouri Territory
land_description: Reaffirmed the 1804 cession.
notes: Reaffirmation of RIT 43; Black Hawk later contested.

name: Treaty with the Cherokee (Cherokee Agency), 1817
nations: Cherokee at Cherokee Agency
land_description: Cherokee cession in the Southeast in exchange for land in Arkansas (early voluntary removal to the West).
notes: Land description from memory [from-memory].

name: Treaty of the Maumee Rapids (Rapids of the Miami of Lake Erie), 1817
nations: Wyandot, Seneca, Delaware, Shawnee, Potawatomi, Ottawa, and Chippewa at Rapids of the Miami of Lake Erie
land_description: Large cession of northwestern Ohio lands; reservations created.
notes: Acreage not retrieved this session.

name: Treaty of St. Mary's with the Miami, 1818
nations: Miami at St. Mary's, Ohio
land_description: Miami cession of central Indiana (the 'New Purchase' area).
notes: Land description from memory [from-memory].

name: Treaty with the Chickasaw (Jackson Purchase), 1818
nations: Chickasaw at Treaty Ground East of Old Town
land_description: Chickasaw cession of western Tennessee and western Kentucky.
notes: Land description from memory [from-memory].

name: Treaty of Saginaw with the Chippewa, 1819
nations: Chippewa at Saginaw
land_description: Cession of ~6 million acres in central Michigan and reservations.
notes: Acreage approx. [from-memory].

name: Treaty of Doak's Stand with the Choctaw, 1820
nations: Choctaw at Treaty Ground Near Doak's Stand on the Natchez Road
land_description: Choctaw cession of roughly 5 million acres in Mississippi in exchange for ~13 million acres west of the Mississippi.
notes: Wikipedia (pointer) for acreage and Jan 8, 1821 effective date; Kappler page from OSU slug. Ratification detail: 1821-01-08 (proclaimed)

name: Treaty of Indian Springs (1821) with the Creeks
nations: Creeks at Indian Springs in the Creek Nation
land_description: Creek cession in Georgia.
notes: Land description from memory [from-memory].

name: Treaty of Chicago, 1821
nations: Ottawa, Chippewa, and Potawatomi at Chicago
land_description: Cession of southwestern Michigan and northern Indiana lands.
notes: Land description from memory [from-memory].

name: Treaty of Moultrie Creek (Florida tribes), 1823
nations: Florida Tribes at Camp on Moultrie Creek, Florida Territory
land_description: Florida tribes ceded claims to Florida in exchange for a ~4 million-acre central-peninsula reservation (not a cession of the reservation).
notes: Reservation ~4 million acres per Wikipedia (pointer); the inadequate reservation preceded Payne's Landing (1832).

name: Treaty of Indian Springs (1825) with the Creeks (McIntosh treaty)
nations: Creeks at Indian Springs
land_description: Cession of virtually all remaining Creek land in Georgia; signed by William McIntosh and a minority faction.
notes: Annulled/superseded by the Treaty of Washington of 1826-01-24 (RIT 144) after Creek National Council protest [from-memory]. Example of a Senate-ratified treaty later abrogated by treaty.

name: Treaty with the Arikara, 1825 (Atkinson-O'Fallon treaties)
nations: Arikara (Ricara) at Arikara Village
land_description: Peace and trade treaty; acknowledged US supremacy; part of the 1825 Upper Missouri treaty series (RIT 126-142).
notes: Stat. page [from-memory]; Kappler page from OSU slug.

name: Treaty of Prairie du Chien (1825)
nations: Sioux, Chippewa, Sauk and Fox, Menominee, Iowa, Winnebago, and Part of Ottawa, Chippewa, and Potawatomi of Illinois at Prairie du Chien, Michigan Territory
land_description: Boundary lines among Sioux, Chippewa, Sauk and Fox, Menominee, Iowa, Winnebago, and others; 'Prairie du Chien Line'; no direct land cession to the US.
notes: Wikipedia (pointer) for proclamation date and content; Kappler page [from-memory]. Ratification detail: 1826-02-06 (proclaimed)

name: Treaty of Washington (1826) with the Creeks
nations: Creeks at Washington, DC
land_description: Annulled the 1825 Indian Springs treaty; new cession of Creek lands in Georgia.
notes: Kappler page from Kappler index (OSU).

name: Treaty of Fond du Lac with the Chippewa, 1826
nations: Chippewa at Fond du Lac of Lake Superior, Michigan Territory
land_description: Boundaries and right to mineral/mining exploration in Chippewa country.
notes: Land description from memory [from-memory].

name: Treaty of Butte des Morts, 1827
nations: Chippewa, Menominee, and Winnebago at Butte des Morts on Fox River, Michigan Territory
land_description: Boundaries among Chippewa, Menominee, Winnebago in Wisconsin.
notes: Land description from memory [from-memory].

name: Treaty of Prairie du Chien (1830) - Sauk, Fox, Sioux, Omaha, Iowa, Oto, Missouri
nations: Sauk and Fox, Sioux (Mdewakanton, Wahpacoota, Wahpeton, Sisseton, Yankton, and Santee), Omaha, Iowa, Oto, and Missouri at Prairie du Chien, Michigan Territory
land_description: Cession of a 'neutral ground' and lands in Iowa/Minnesota/Missouri region.
notes: Dated 1830-07-15 (pre-Removal-Act is 1830-05-28; era assigned by treaty-cluster). Kappler page [from-memory]; land description [from-memory].

name: Treaty of Dancing Rabbit Creek with the Choctaw, 1830
nations: Choctaw at Dancing Rabbit Creek
land_description: Cession of the Choctaw Nation's remaining lands in Mississippi (~11 million acres) in exchange for land in Indian Territory; first removal treaty under the Indian Removal Act; Art. 14 allowed families to remain with 640-acre allotments.
notes: OSU TTD notes one paragraph was not ratified. Wikipedia gives ~15 million acres received in Indian Territory. Date conflict between proclamation and Senate consent sources [disputed]. The supplementary-articles cite 7 Stat. 340 is [unverified] (V2: govinfo page 340 not found). Ratification detail: 1831-02-24 (proclaimed); Senate consent date 1831-02-25 per Wikipedia (conflict)

name: Treaty of Cusseta (Treaty of Washington) with the Creeks, 1832
nations: Creeks at Washington, DC
land_description: Cession of all Creek land east of the Mississippi (Alabama); allotments of sections to chiefs and half-sections to families.
notes: Wikipedia (pointer): negotiated at Cusseta then signed in Washington; ~$350,000 paid.

name: Treaty of Payne's Landing with the Seminole, 1832
nations: Seminole at Payne's Landing, Ocklawaha River, Florida Territory
land_description: Seminole agreement to move west of the Mississippi to the Creek Nation if a delegation approved; basis for US removal claims leading to the Second Seminole War.
notes: Seminole leaders later disputed that the delegation had authority to bind the nation [from-memory]. Ratification detail: 1834-04 (Senate); proclaimed 1834-04-12

name: Black Hawk Purchase (Treaty of Fort Armstrong), 1832
nations: Sauk and Fox at Fort Armstrong, Rock Island, Illinois
land_description: Sauk and Meskwaki cession of a strip of eastern Iowa (~50 miles wide) after the Black Hawk War, with Keokuk's Reserve.
notes: $640,000 payment (~$0.11/acre) per Wikipedia (pointer). Ratification detail: 1833-02-13 (proclaimed; Senate-consent date not located)

name: Treaty of Pontotoc Creek with the Chickasaw, 1832
nations: Chickasaw at Pontitock Creek, Chickasaw Nation
land_description: Cession of all remaining Chickasaw land in Mississippi; confirmed by the 1834 Treaty of Washington (RIT 191).
notes: Chickasaw paid for own removal from land-sale proceeds (Wikipedia, pointer). Unratified 1830 Franklin treaty precedes (see TLA-U-FRANKLIN).

name: Treaty of Fort Gibson with the Seminole, 1833
nations: Seminole at Fort Gibson, Arkansas River
land_description: Seminole delegation's approval of Western lands; used by the US to treat Payne's Landing as binding.
notes: Kappler page from Kappler index (OSU).

name: Treaty of Chicago with the Chippewa, Ottawa, Potawatomi, 1833
nations: United Chippewa, Ottawa, and Potawatomi at Chicago, Illinois
land_description: Cession of ~5 million acres in Illinois, Wisconsin, Michigan Territories; land in Kansas Territory promised; removal by 1838.
notes: Wikipedia (pointer) for acreage and ratification; ceded the last large tract north of the Ohio and east of the Mississippi per that source. Ratification detail: 1835-02-21 (proclaimed; Senate-consent date not located)

name: Treaty of Camp Holmes with the Comanche, Wichita and others, 1835
nations: Comanche, Wichita, Cherokee, Muscogee, Choctaw, Osage, Seneca, and Quapaw at Camp Holmes, Muscogee Nation
land_description: Peace and trade; not a cession; first treaty with Comanche and Wichita on the southern Plains.
notes: First-treaty characterization [from-memory]; Stat./Kappler pages verified.

name: Treaty of New Echota with the Cherokee, 1835
nations: Cherokee at New Echota, Georgia
land_description: Cession of all Cherokee lands east of the Mississippi in exchange for 7 million acres west plus 800,000 acres; basis for the Trail of Tears; signed by the Treaty Party, not the Cherokee National Council or Principal Chief John Ross.
notes: Acreage east of the Mississippi not stated in sources read; Royce polygons would supply. OSU TTD record carries Cherokee Nation Attorney General note about successor-in-interest (UKB). Wikipedia: 20 signatories. Ratification detail: 1836-05 (Senate, one-vote margin); proclaimed 1836-05-23

name: Treaty of Washington (1836) with the Ottawa and Chippewa
nations: Ottawa and Chippewa at Washington, DC
land_description: Cession of roughly the northwestern Lower Peninsula and eastern Upper Peninsula of Michigan (~13.8 million acres).
notes: Acreage approx. 13.8 million [from-memory]. Senate amended the treaty; tribal acceptance of amendments contested [from-memory]; basis for the 2000 Consent Decree on fishing rights [from-memory].

name: Treaty of Doaksville with the Choctaw and Chickasaw, 1837
nations: Choctaw and Chickasaw at Doaksville near Fort Towson, Choctaw Country
land_description: Chickasaw settled within the Choctaw Nation (Chickasaw District) in Indian Territory for $530,000.
notes: Stat. cite in vol. 11 (published late) per Stat. vol. 11 index; Wikipedia (pointer) for payment.

name: Treaty of St. Peters (1837) with the Chippewa
nations: Chippewa at St. Peters, Wisconsin Territory
land_description: Chippewa cession of lands in Wisconsin and Minnesota with reserved usufructuary rights (hunting, fishing, gathering).
notes: Basis for the 1999 Supreme Court decision Minnesota v. Mille Lacs Band, 526 U.S. 172 (1999) [from-memory].

name: Treaty of Buffalo Creek with the New York Indians, 1838
nations: New York Indians, Six Nations (St. Regis, Seneca, Cayuga, Oneida, Tuscarora, and Onondaga) at Buffalo Creek, New York
land_description: Sale of Seneca lands in western New York and removal to Kansas; later compromised by 1842 and 1857 treaties.
notes: Fraud and coercion alleged; Tonawanda Band's repudiation led to 1857 treaty (RIT 305) [from-memory].

name: Treaty of La Pointe (1842) with the Chippewa of the Mississippi and Lake Superior
nations: Chippewa of the Mississippi and Lake Superior at La Pointe of Lake Superior, Wisconsin Territory
land_description: Cession of Lake Superior copper country in Wisconsin and Michigan with retained usufructuary rights.
notes: Kappler page [from-memory]. Basis for Lac Courte Oreilles v. Voigt litigation [from-memory].

name: Treaty of Washington (1846) with the Cherokee
nations: Cherokee at Washington, DC
land_description: Reconciled factions (Old Settlers, Treaty Party, Ross Party) in Indian Territory.
notes: Kappler page [from-memory]. Ratification detail: 1846-08-08 (Senate consent; read from the Stat. margin by V2).

name: Treaty with the Navajo (Canyon de Chelly / Chuska Valley), 1849
nations: Navajo at Valley of Cheille
land_description: Navajo acknowledgment of US jurisdiction; boundaries; peace.
notes: Stat. page [from-memory]; Stat. vol. 9 OCR index prints 971 [disputed]. Kappler page [from-memory].

name: Treaty with the Utah (Abiquiu), 1849
nations: Utah at Abiquin [Abiquiu], New Mexico Territory
land_description: Ute peace and US jurisdiction in New Mexico Territory.
notes: Kappler pages 585-587 per OSU comprehensive index. Ratification detail: 1850-09-09 (Senate consent; read from the Stat. margin by V2).

name: Treaty of Traverse des Sioux (Sisseton and Wahpeton), 1851
nations: Sioux (Sisseton and Wahpeton) at Traverse des Sioux on the Minnesota River, Minnesota Territory
land_description: Cession of ~21 million acres in Minnesota, Iowa, South Dakota; reservations along the Minnesota River.
notes: Senate struck Section 3 (Wikipedia, pointer); Kappler page [from-memory]. Ratification detail: 1852-06-23 (Senate consent (with amendments); read from the Stat. margin by V2).

name: Treaty of Mendota (Mdewakanton and Wahpekute), 1851
nations: Sioux (Mdewakanton and Wahpahkoota) at Mendota, Minnesota Territory
land_description: Cession of lands in Minnesota/Iowa; with Traverse des Sioux roughly 24 million acres combined per Wikipedia.
notes: Kappler page [from-memory]. Combined-acreage claim from Wikipedia (pointer). 1862 Dakota War and 1863 forfeiture act followed [from-memory].

name: Treaty of Fort Laramie (Horse Creek), 1851
nations: Sioux (Lakota), Cheyenne, Arapaho, Crow, Assiniboine, Mandan, Hidatsa, Arikara (Gros Ventre and Shoshone attended)
land_description: Defined tribal territories on the northern Plains (Arkansas to Missouri Rivers); safe passage on Oregon Trail, roads and forts; annuities. Not a land cession by the Lakota.
notes: Senate reduced annuity period from 50 to 10 years (Art. 5); UNL Treaties Portal holds a proposed corrected text reflecting unpublished Senate changes. This treaty does NOT appear in the NARA RIT table as extracted (no 1851-09-17 row between RIT 258/259) - verify NARA numbering. Stat./Kappler pages from Wikipedia pointer and Stat. vol. 11 index. Ratification detail: 1852-05 (Senate, with amendment) [from-memory]

name: Treaty with the Apache (Santa Fe), 1852
nations: Apache at Santa Fe, New Mexico Territory
land_description: Apache acknowledgment of US jurisdiction; peace.
notes: Kappler page [from-memory].

name: Treaty of Fort Atkinson with the Comanche, Kiowa, Apache, 1853
nations: Comanche, Kiowa, and Apache at Fort Atkinson, Indian Territory
land_description: Safe passage on Santa Fe Trail; recognition of right to establish roads and forts.
notes: Kappler page [from-memory].

name: Treaty with the Rogue River Indians (Table Rock), 1853
nations: Rogue River at Table Rock near Rogue River, Oregon Territory
land_description: Cession of Rogue River Valley lands; temporary reservation at Table Rock.
notes: Kappler page [from-memory]. Followed by the Rogue River War and removal to Siletz/Grand Ronde [from-memory].

name: Treaty of Medicine Creek, 1854
nations: Nisqualli, Puyallup, et al. at Medicine Creek, Washington Territory
land_description: Cession of ~2.24 million acres of Puget Sound lands by the Nisqually, Puyallup, Steilacoom, Squaxin Island, S'Homamish, Stehchass, T'Peeksin, Squi-aitl, and Sa-heh-wamish in exchange for three small reservations; reserved fishing rights.
notes: Acreage per Wikipedia (pointer); Kappler page [from-memory]. First of the Stevens treaties. Basis of the Boldt decision (United States v. Washington, 384 F. Supp. 312 (W.D. Wash. 1974)) [from-memory]. Ratification detail: 1855-03-03 (Senate resolution; verified in 10 Stat. 1132 by V2); President ratified 1855-04-10

name: Treaty of Point Elliott, 1855
nations: Dwamish, Suquamish, et al. at Point Elliott, Washington Territory
land_description: Cession of Puget Sound lands (Point Pully to the British boundary) by Duwamish, Suquamish, Snoqualmie, Snohomish, Lummi, Skagit, Swinomish and others; reservations at Port Madison, Tulalip, Swinomish, Lummi.
notes: Wikipedia (pointer): no reservations for Duwamish, Skagit, Snohomish, Snoqualmie; Stat. cite per Wikipedia; Kappler page [from-memory]. Duwamish remain federally unrecognized [from-memory]. Ratification detail: 1859-03-08 (Senate)

name: Treaty of Point No Point, 1855
nations: S'klallam (Clallam; Various Divisions), Sokokomish (Twana), Toanhooch (Twana), and Chimakum at Point No Point, Suquamish Head, Washington Territory
land_description: Cession of northern Kitsap and Olympic Peninsulas by S'Klallam, Chimakum, Skokomish (Twana); $60,000.
notes: Stat. cite per Wikipedia (pointer); Kappler page [from-memory].

name: Treaty of Neah Bay (Makah), 1855
nations: Makah at Neah Bay, Washington Territory
land_description: Makah cession of much of their lands; reserved right to fish, whale and seal at usual and accustomed grounds.
notes: Stat./Kappler pages [from-memory].

name: Treaty of Walla Walla (Cayuse, Umatilla, Walla Walla), 1855
nations: Walla Walla, Cayuse, and Umatilla at Camp Stevens, Walla Walla Valley
land_description: Cession of ~45,000 sq mi (per Wikipedia, pointer) for the Umatilla Reservation; reserved off-reservation rights.
notes: Acreage not entered: 45,000 sq mi ~ 28.8 million acres is derived and not independently sourced. Stat. page agrees with Stat. vol. 12 OCR index; Kappler page [from-memory]. Ratification detail: 1859-03-08 (Senate consent); proclaimed 1859-04-11

name: Yakama Treaty, 1855
nations: Yakima and Confederated Tribes at Camp Stevens, Walla Walla Valley
land_description: Cession of ~10 million acres by 14 confederated tribes and bands; Yakama Reservation; reserved rights to fish at usual and accustomed places (Art. 3).
notes: Acreage ~10-11 million [from-memory, not entered]; Stat. page [from-memory] (OCR index prints 961 [disputed]); Kappler page [from-memory]. Subject of Washington v. Washington State Commercial Passenger Fishing Vessel Ass'n, 443 U.S. 658 (1979) and Cougar Den v. Washington State Dept. of Licensing (2019) [from-memory].

name: Nez Perce Treaty of 1855
nations: Nez Perces at Camp Stevens, Walla Walla Valley
land_description: Cession of ~7.5 million acres; reservation of ~7.7 million acres in present Idaho/Oregon/Washington.
notes: Acreages [from-memory, not entered]. Reduced ~90% by the 1863 'Steal Treaty' (RIT 323).

name: Treaty with the Tribes of Middle Oregon (Warm Springs), 1855
nations: Walla Walla and Wasco at Columbia River, Oregon Territory
land_description: Cession of Columbia River lands; Warm Springs Reservation.
notes: Stat./Kappler [from-memory].

name: Treaty of Olympia / Quinault River (Quinault, Quileute), 1855-56
nations: Quinaielt [Quinault] and Quileute at Olympia and on the Quinaielt [Quinault] River, Washington Territory (second date 1856-01-25)
land_description: Cession of Olympic Peninsula coast lands; Quinault Reservation; reserved fishing rights.
notes: Stat. page agrees with Stat. vol. 12 OCR index; Kappler page [from-memory]. Signed in two sessions 1855-07-01 (Olympia) and 1856-01-25 (Quinault River).

name: Hellgate Treaty (Bitterroot Salish, Pend d'Oreille, Kootenai), 1855
nations: Flathead, Kutenai, and Upper Pend d'Oreilles at Hell Gate Treaty Grounds, Bitter Root Valley, Washington Territory
land_description: Cession of lands from the Rocky Mountain crest to the Clark Fork/Bitterroot; Flathead Indian Reservation; $120,000.
notes: Wikipedia (pointer) for ratification/proclamation. Stat./Kappler pages [from-memory]. Region assigned Pacific NW per treaty-making jurisdiction (Washington Territory), though lands are in present Montana; map as Northern Rockies. Ratification detail: 1859-03-08 (Senate); proclaimed 1859-04-18

name: Treaty of Detroit (1855) with the Ottawa and Chippewa of Michigan
nations: Ottawa and Chippewa (Sault Ste. Marie Bands, Grand River Bands, Grand Traverse Bands, Little Traverse Bands, and Mackinac Bands) at Detroit, Michigan
land_description: Reserved tracts for Ottawa and Chippewa bands in northern Lower Peninsula; relinquished 1836 treaty claims.
notes: Stat. page per Stat. vol. 11 OCR index; Kappler page [from-memory].

name: Treaty of La Pointe (1854) with the Chippewa of Lake Superior and the Mississippi
nations: Chippewa of Lake Superior and the Mississippi at La Pointe, Wisconsin
land_description: Cession of Minnesota Arrowhead lands; created Bad River, Red Cliff, Lac Courte Oreilles, Lac du Flambeau, Fond du Lac, Grand Portage, and other reservations.

notes: Stat. page per Stat. vol. 11 OCR index; Kappler page [from-memory].

name: Treaty with the Pawnee (Table Creek), 1857
nations: Pawnee at Table Creek, Nebraska Territory
land_description: Pawnee cession of Nebraska lands, retaining a reservation on the Loup River.
notes: Kappler page [from-memory].

name: Treaty of Tonawanda Band of Seneca, 1857
nations: Seneca (Tonawanda) at Tonawanda Reservation, Genesee County, New York
land_description: Relinquished claims to Kansas lands in exchange for repurchase of the Tonawanda Reservation in New York.
notes: Stat. page per Stat. vol. 12 OCR index (OCR unreliable); Kappler page not verified. Ratification detail: 1858-06-04 (Senate consent; read from the Stat. margin by V2).

name: Treaty with the Yankton Sioux, 1858
nations: Sioux (Yankton) at Washington, DC
land_description: Cession of ~11 million acres of eastern South Dakota in exchange for a ~430,000-acre reservation.
notes: Acreage figures [from-memory, not entered]; Kappler page [from-memory].

name: Treaty of Fort Wise (Arapaho and Cheyenne of the Upper Arkansas), 1861
nations: Arapaho and Cheyenne (of the Upper Arkansas) at Fort Wise, Kansas Territory
land_description: Cession of most of the 1851 Fort Laramie territory for a small reservation at Sand Creek; signed by a minority of chiefs.
notes: Stat. page [from-memory] (Stat. vol. 12 OCR index prints 1168 [disputed]); Kappler page [from-memory]. Precedes the 1864 Sand Creek Massacre; legitimacy contested by Cheyenne chiefs not present [from-memory].

name: Nez Perce Treaty of 1863 ('Steal Treaty')
nations: Nez Perces at Valley of the Lapwai, Washington Territory
land_description: Reduced the 1855 reservation by ~90% (about 6.9 million acres ceded), signed by Lapwai faction; Joseph's band did not sign.
notes: Stat. page per Stat. vol. 14 OCR index; acreage and Kappler page [from-memory]. Ratification detail: 1867-04-17 (Senate consent; read from the Stat. margin by V2).

name: Treaty of Fort Bridger (1863) with the Eastern Shoshone
nations: Shoshoni (Eastern) at Fort Bridger, Utah Territory
land_description: Peace; right-of-way and boundaries for Eastern Shoshone territory (Wyoming/Utah).
notes: Stat./Kappler [from-memory]; ratified 1869 [from-memory].

name: Treaty of Ruby Valley (Western Shoshone), 1863
nations: Shoshoni (Western) at Ruby Valley, Nevada Territory
land_description: Peace and friendship; defined ~40,000 sq mi of Western Shoshone territory in Nevada/Utah/Idaho/California; did not cede land title (Western Shoshone position).
notes: Stat. cite per Wikipedia (pointer); Kappler page [from-memory]. US v. Dann, 470 U.S. 39 (1985) held aboriginal title extinguished by payment into the ICC judgment account; Western Shoshone dispute this [from-memory].

name: Treaty of Box Elder (Northwestern Shoshone), 1863
nations: Shoshoni (Northwestern) at Box Elder, Utah Territory
land_description: Peace and right-of-way; annuities.
notes: Stat. page per Stat. vol. 13 OCR index; Kappler page [from-memory]. Ratification detail: 1864-03-07 (Senate consent (with amendment); read from the Stat. margin by V2).

name: Treaty with the Klamath, Modoc and Yahooskin Band of Snake, 1864
nations: Klamath, Modoc, and Snake (Yahooskin) at Klamath Lake, Oregon
land_description: Cession of ~20 million acres in south-central Oregon; Klamath Reservation (terminated 1954).
notes: Stat. page per Stat. vol. 16 OCR index (listed there as an 'agreement' entry); acreage and Kappler page [from-memory]. Klamath Termination Act 1954 [from-memory]. Ratification detail: 1866-07-02 (Senate consent (with amendments); read from the Stat. margin by V2).

name: Treaty of Little Arkansas (Cheyenne and Arapaho), 1865
nations: Cheyenne and Arapaho at Little Arkansas River, Kansas
land_description: Southern Cheyenne and Arapaho cession after Sand Creek; reservation in Kansas/Indian Territory; reparations for Sand Creek survivors.
notes: Stat. page per Stat. vol. 14 OCR index; Kappler page [from-memory]. Replaced by Medicine Lodge (1867).

name: Reconstruction Treaty with the Seminole, 1866
nations: Seminole at Washington, DC
land_description: Seminole ceded the Western Seminole reservation; new lands in Creek Nation; emancipation/freedmen provisions.
notes: Stat. page per Stat. vol. 14 OCR index; Kappler page [from-memory]. Reconstruction treaties penalised tribes that allied with the Confederacy (see UNL Confederate treaties of 1861).

name: Reconstruction Treaty with the Choctaw and Chickasaw, 1866
nations: Choctaw and Chickasaw at Washington, DC
land_description: Cession of the 'Leased District'; freedmen provisions; railroad rights-of-way.
notes: Stat. page per Stat. vol. 14 OCR index; Kappler page [from-memory].

name: Reconstruction Treaty with the Creeks, 1866
nations: Creeks at Washington, DC
land_description: Cession of western half of the Creek domain; freedmen provisions.
notes: Stat. page per Stat. vol. 14 OCR index; Kappler page [from-memory].

name: Reconstruction Treaty with the Cherokee, 1866
nations: Cherokee at Washington, DC
land_description: Cession of the Cherokee Outlet access; freedmen citizenship; railroad rights-of-way; land for other tribes.
notes: Stat. page per Stat. vol. 14 OCR index; Kappler page [from-memory]. Ratification detail: 1866-07-27 (Senate consent (with amendments); read from the Stat. margin by V2).

name: Treaty of Medicine Lodge (Kiowa and Comanche), 1867
nations: Kiowa and Comanche at Medicine Lodge Creek, Kansas
land_description: Surrender of ~60,000 sq mi in exchange for a ~3 million-acre reservation in southwestern Indian Territory.
notes: Proclaimed 1868-08-25. Wikipedia (pointer): tribes never ratified by the required three-fourths adult male vote. Undermined by Jerome Agreement and Lone Wolf v. Hitchcock, 187 U.S. 553 (1903). Ratification detail: 1868-07-25 (Senate)

name: Treaty of Medicine Lodge (Kiowa, Comanche and Apache), 1867
nations: Kiowa, Comanche, and Apache at Medicine Lodge Creek, Kansas
land_description: Kiowa-Apache (Plains Apache) joined the Kiowa-Comanche reservation.
notes: Proclaimed 1868-08-25. Ratification detail: 1868-07-25 (Senate)

name: Treaty of Medicine Lodge (Cheyenne and Arapaho), 1867
nations: Cheyenne and Arapaho at Medicine Lodge Creek, Kansas
land_description: Southern Cheyenne and Arapaho reservation of ~4.3 million acres south of Kansas; right to hunt north of the Arkansas while buffalo lasted.
notes: Reservation of ~4.3 million acres retained (Wikipedia, pointer); acreage_ceded left blank. Proclaimed 1868-08-19. Ratification detail: 1868-07-25 (Senate)

name: Treaty with the Ute (Kit Carson Treaty), 1868
nations: Ute (multiple bands) at Washington, DC
land_description: Ute Reservation in western Colorado (treaty sometimes called the Kit Carson Treaty [from-memory]); later reduced by the 1873 Brunot Agreement and 1880 agreement.
notes: Kappler page [from-memory].

name: Treaty of Fort Laramie (1868) - Lakota (Sioux) and Arapaho
nations: Sioux (Brule, Oglala, Miniconjou, Yanktonai, Hunkpapa, Blackfeet, Cuthead, Two Kettle, Sans Arcs, and Santee) and Arapaho at Fort Laramie, Dakota Territory
land_description: Established the Great Sioux Reservation (including the Black Hills) and 'unceded Indian territory' (Art. 16, ~33 million acres under the 1851 treaty plus ~25 million additional per Wikipedia); abandonment of Bozeman Trail forts; Art. 12 required three-fourths adult male consent to future cessions.
notes: Stat. page verified by V2: 15 Stat. 635 (govinfo page 635; Senate Feb. 16, 1869; proclaimed Feb. 24, 1869). The Stat. vol. 15 OCR index misprints 685; Kappler page 998 per Wikipedia (pointer). NARA lists it as Treaty No. 369 on microfilm M668 roll 16, NAID 299803 per archives.gov, but the NARA catalog-links table shows NAID 183517089 (conflict between NAID forms). Ratification detail: 1869-02-16 (Senate)

name: Treaty with the Crow, 1868
nations: Crows at Fort Laramie, Dakota Territory
land_description: Crow Reservation in southern Montana; cession of earlier 1851 treaty territory.
notes: Kappler page: Wikipedia (pointer) cites pp. 1008-1011 for related material; verify.

name: Treaty with the Northern Cheyenne and Northern Arapaho (Fort Laramie), 1868
nations: Cheyenne (Northern) and Arapaho (Northern) at Fort Laramie, Dakota Territory
land_description: Permitted Northern Cheyenne and Arapaho to settle with the Southern bands or on the Sioux Reservation.
notes: Kappler page [from-memory]; consistent with Wikipedia (pointer) range.

name: Treaty of Bosque Redondo (Fort Sumner) with the Navajo, 1868
nations: Navaho [Navajo] at Fort Sumner, New Mexico Territory
land_description: Ended the Long Walk captivity; established a Navajo Reservation (~3.5 million acres) in the Four Corners region; right to return home.
notes: Acreage [from-memory, not entered]; Kappler page [from-memory].

name: Fort Bridger Treaty of 1868 (Eastern Shoshone and Bannock)
nations: Shoshoni (Eastern Band) and Bannock at Fort Bridger, Utah Territory
land_description: Wind River Reservation (Eastern Shoshone) and Fort Hall Reservation (Bannock); Bannock reservation reduced by later executive order/agreements.
notes: Dates per Wikipedia (pointer); Kappler page [from-memory]. Described there as the last treaty council to establish a reservation. Ratification detail: 1869-02-16 (Senate); proclaimed 1869-02-24

kappler_cite: none (not in Kappler Vol. II treaties; see Heizer 1972)
notes: Letter A-R follows Heizer (1972) schedule. U.S. commissioner(s): McKee. Tribal names as printed in Heizer, in 1850s spellings; present-day nation identification needs tribal consultation. Senate rejected all 18 in secret session 1852-07-08 (Heizer, Mechoopda); Prologue (NARA) article says 1852-07-02 [disputed]. Injunction of secrecy lifted 1905-01-18. Total proposed acreage not stated in Heizer; Mechoopda page says 'more than eight million acres' for all 18 (self-described tribal source).

name: Treaty with the Sioux (Pike), 1805
nations: Sioux (Dakota)
land_description: Lieutenant Zebulon Pike's 1805 agreement for military-post sites at the Minnesota/Mississippi confluence (St. Anthony Falls area).
notes: Kappler page from OSU URL slug (p. 1031). Ratification status: treated as unratified because the OSU/Kappler record sits in the unratified-document range (p. 1031); whether the Senate ever acted on it was not verified [unverified]. Date [from-memory].

name: Treaty with the Cherokee, 1835-03-14 (unratified)
nations: Cherokee
land_description: Washington negotiation preceding New Echota; listed as unratified in Kappler's index.
notes: Kappler index entry 'Mar 14, 1835, unratified (1041)' read on the OSU Kappler's Index page.

name: Franklin Treaty with the Chickasaw, 1830 (unratified)
nations: Chickasaw
land_description: Conditional cession of Chickasaw lands in Mississippi contingent on finding suitable western land.
notes: Per Wikipedia (pointer) the Franklin Treaty was never ratified; precedes Pontotoc Creek (RIT 173). Date and Kappler citation not verified. [single-source: V2 found Wikipedia only; it gives Aug. 27, 1830, consistent with 1830-08; date_signed_basis stays from-memory]

name: Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo (US-Mexico), 1848
nations: United States; Mexico (Native nations not parties)
land_description: Mexican Cession (California, Nevada, Utah, most of Arizona, New Mexico, parts of Colorado and Wyoming). Art. XI committed US to restrain 'Indian' raids into Mexico (annulled by 1853 Gadsden/Mesilla treaty); Art. IX and Querétaro Protocol on property of Mexican citizens.
notes: Not a treaty with Native nations; included because it transferred sovereignty claims over Native lands without their consent. Pueblo and other Indigenous land rights issues (Pueblo Lands Act 1924 [from-memory]) arise under Spanish/Mexican law. Native nations were not parties. Detail from Wikipedia (pointer); read primary text before publication. Ratification detail: 1848-03-10 (US Senate); proclaimed 1848-07-04

name: Treaty of Cession of Alaska (US-Russia), 1867
nations: United States; Russia (Alaska Native peoples not parties)
land_description: Russian cession of Alaska; Alaska Native peoples' land title unaddressed except through later statutes (ANCSA 1971).
notes: Stat. vol. 15 index lists '1867 Mar 30 Russia, 539'. Art. III distinguishing 'uncivilized native tribes' [from-memory]. Not a treaty with Native nations; Alaska had no US treaties with Native nations.

name: Treaty of Friendship, Commerce and Navigation (US-Kingdom of Hawai'i), 1849
nations: Hawaiian Kingdom; United States
land_description: Recognition of the Hawaiian Kingdom as an independent state (foreign-relations treaty). Hawai'i is outside the US-Native nation treaty corpus; included as clearly labeled context.
notes: Stat. vol. 9 index note: the list excludes the Hawaiian Islands treaty of Dec 20, 1849, p. 977, as a treaty with a nation rather than a tribe. Only the citation is confirmed.

name: Trade and Intercourse Act (Nonintercourse Act), 1790
nations: n/a (Congress)
land_description: Declared Indian land sales valid only if made at a public treaty under US authority.
notes: Wikipedia (pointer) gives 1 Stat. 137; 1834 version at 4 Stat. 729 (25 U.S.C. 177). Date [from-memory].

name: Indian Removal Act, 1830
nations: n/a (Congress)
land_description: Authorized exchange of Indian lands in states for lands west of the Mississippi.
notes: Wikipedia (pointer): Pub. L. 21-148; Senate 28-19, House 101-97 (one footnote gives 102-97).

name: Indian Appropriation Act of March 3, 1871 (end of treaty-making)
nations: n/a (Congress)
land_description: Proviso: no Indian nation or tribe shall be acknowledged as an independent nation or power with whom the US may contract by treaty; pre-1871 treaty obligations preserved.
notes: Source credit read on Cornell LII: R.S. 2079; derived from Act of Mar. 3, 1871, ch. 120, sec. 1, 16 Stat. 566; 1988 amendment Pub. L. 100-647, 102 Stat. 3641.

name: Brunot Agreement with the Ute, 1873-74
nations: Ute (Colorado bands)
land_description: Ute cession of the San Juan Mountains mining region in Colorado.
notes: All fields except the existence of the agreement are [from-memory]; needs verification. Ratification detail: 1874-04-29 [from-memory]

name: Black Hills Agreement (Act of February 28, 1877) - Lakota
nations: Lakota (Sioux), Cheyenne, Arapaho
land_description: Unilateral Act of Congress taking the Black Hills and unceded territory after the 1876 war, without the three-fourths consent required by Art. 12 of the 1868 treaty.
notes: United States v. Sioux Nation of Indians, 448 U.S. 371 (1980) held the taking required just compensation ($15.5 million plus interest per Wikipedia, pointer). The Lakota have refused the award. Stat. cite [from-memory].

name: General Allotment (Dawes) Act, 1887
nations: n/a (Congress)
land_description: Allotment of reservation land in 160/80/40-acre parcels; surplus lands opened to settlement. Indian-held land fell from ~138 million acres (1887) to ~48 million acres (1934) per Wikipedia (pointer).
notes: Ended further allotment with the Indian Reorganization Act of 1934 (Wikipedia, pointer).

name: Jerome Agreement (Kiowa, Comanche, Apache), 1892 / Act of 1900
nations: Kiowa, Comanche, Apache
land_description: Cession of most of the Medicine Lodge reservation; 160-acre allotments; ~2.9 million acres reduced to ~3,000 acres by the end of allotment (Wikipedia, pointer).
notes: Signed by 456 of 639 members (Wikipedia, pointer) - the Medicine Lodge three-fourths requirement was not met. Lone Wolf v. Hitchcock, 187 U.S. 553 (1903) held Congress has plenary power to abrogate treaty provisions. Ratification detail: 1900-06-06 [from-memory]

name: Executive Order creating the Hopi Reservation, 1882
nations: Hopi (and Navajo residing there)
land_description: Executive order reservation in northeastern Arizona (the 1882 Hopi Reservation).
stat_cite: n/a (executive order; Kappler Vol. I, executive orders section) [from-memory]
notes: Wikipedia (pointer) states the Hopi reservation was created by an executive order of President Arthur in 1882. Date and compilation location [from-memory]. 25 U.S.C. 211 (Act of May 25, 1918, 40 Stat. 570) later barred new or enlarged reservations in AZ and NM except by Act of Congress.

name: Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act (ANCSA), 1971
nations: Alaska Native peoples (shareholders of 12 regional + 200+ village corporations)
land_description: Extinguished aboriginal title and claims in Alaska in exchange for ~44 million acres and $962.5 million (Wikipedia gives $963 million in one place); created 12 land-owning regional corporations (plus a 13th non-land-owning).
notes: Natives retained up to ~44 million acres (not a cession figure; acreage_ceded left blank). Settlement by statute rather than treaty; criticized as illegitimate by some Alaska Natives (Wikipedia, pointer). Tribal consultation required before publication.

name: Maine Indian Claims Settlement Act, 1980
nations: Passamaquoddy, Penobscot, Maliseet (Houlton Band)
land_description: Statutory settlement of Nonintercourse Act land claims in Maine; $81.5 million settlement per Wikipedia (Nonintercourse Act page, pointer).
notes: Settlement amount verified via Wikipedia (pointer); Stat. cite and date verified by V2 (94 Stat. 1785, approved 1980-10-10); exact tribal names [from-memory].

name: Apology Resolution (Pub. L. 103-150), 1993
nations: Native Hawaiians
land_description: Acknowledged the 1893 overthrow of the Kingdom of Hawai'i and that Native Hawaiians never directly relinquished claims to sovereignty over their national lands; settles no claims.
notes: Hawaii v. Office of Hawaiian Affairs, 556 U.S. 163 (2009) held the resolution's whereas clauses have no binding legal effect (Wikipedia pointer; case cite [from-memory]).
